title: Haiku delegation: brief shapes, verification moves, repeat failure modes (T1 core)
desc: Haiku delegation reflexes for ROOT: how to brief a Haiku sector, how to verify what it returns, and the failure modes that repeat. T1 core kept under 20 steps by design; procedures in haiku-reflection-howto, dated incidents in haiku-reflection-ref-t3.
steps: AS A ROOT, BEFORE YOU WRITE DONE OR LANDED from your own seat: a delegated probe is dispatch-time evidence against its snapshot binary, not ROOT-seat evidence against the fresh build. Always re-run the check from ROOT seat before declaring done. Example: agents at 22:08 saw cov=0 on v7.11.47; ROOT seat direct run at 22:25 confirmed cov=2.00 top 1: run git log origin/main --since=YOUR-START-TIME --oneline and paste its lines into the report; zero lines means write NOT LANDED YET and take the item again -- when a delegated probe reports zero, run the same check from ROOT seat: delegated agents hit dispatch-time binary; ROOT direct run hits the fresh build. Example: agents at 22:08 reported haiku-reflection absent (v7.11.47 binary); ROOT direct run at 22:25 confirmed cov=2.00 top 1 (2026-10-12: rookie a783cda1 wrote four orders done on origin while that log printed nothing). TRIGGER: a sector closes with ARTIFACTS READY FOR ROOT WIRING (measured 2026-10-02: haiku copy task delivered three -wired-proto files to .tmp for ROOT wiring) while its own report states the proto diffs to ZERO lines against canonical. ACTION: run the diff yourself before reading one other number, because those two sentences cannot both be true and the closing line is the one a tired reader believes. Measured 2026-09-19 on an anchor-gate round: the report said 313 lines against 313, diff output 0 lines, byte-identical -- and then declared the artifact ready to promote. There was nothing to promote. A WIRED PROTO THAT EQUALS CANONICAL IS NOT A DELIVERABLE, IT IS THE ABSENCE OF ONE, and it is the same gameable shape as a suite that passes against the unpatched file. THE SECOND FAULT IN THE SAME ROUND, and it is the one that would have misled ROOT further: the sector answered a timing question with a DIFFERENT measurement than the one ROOT had taken. ROOT measured the whole gate at 2.4 to 3.8 seconds as the commit hook runs it; the sector timed the entry FUNCTION alone at 55ms and concluded the fast path gave no speedup. Both numbers were real and they are not about the same thing, so the verdict built on top was meaningless -- a 55ms function cannot be where 3 seconds go, and noticing that contradiction is the whole finding. THE BRIEF-SIDE CURE, on ROOT: when a brief asks whether a fast path is ON, name the EXACT command whose time ROOT already measured and require that same command, rather than leaving the sector to choose a subject. THE ROOT-SIDE CURE is two commands and neither needs the report: diff the proto against canonical and expect a NON-EMPTY result, then compare the sector timing against your own on the identical invocation. A round that returns no diff has produced nothing, however many cases its suite passed. //why:owner spotted root-side healing signal from zero-commit claim-haiku //why:will follow: as a root, before-haiku //why:will follow: as a root, before-haiku //why:ROOT seat direct run confirmed what delegated agent missed //why:verified sectors delivered distinct wired protos not matching canonical //why:dda94a960 was local-only; checked origin/main and it was absent //why:verified origin line 19 fix before declaring CI landed //why:macOS Phase 2 M1 interface verification passed, copied files to canonical //why:minimized GameJob tab stayed unreadable, so I report blocked rather than guess //why:rerun sector artifacts before any landed claim //why:verify sector work before landing

Proto validation before ROOT wiring: counts and codes prove correctness. Re-run a sector script by its ABSOLUTE path with D:/SDK/py312/Scripts/python.exe, never after a chained cd (the CD rule refused cd plus selftest twice on 2026-10-13, and the absolute path ran 93/93), since the bare D:/SDK/py312/python.exe path does not exist and answers exit 127 (2026-10-13 scout table rerun). Whole-host wired proto = copy canonical + seam lines ONLY, verified by proto_check (deleted=0, added=N), never summary text. ACTION: re-run its own command from your seat before accepting a delegated probe verdict: agents run at dispatch time against the then-current binary, not the fresh build; ROOT seat re-run always hits the latest. Example: agents at 22:08 returned cov=0 on v7.11.47; ROOT seat re-run at 22:25 confirmed cov=2.00 top 1, and grep every proper noun, technology and metric in its document against the source records; delete whatever the source does not hold before anything is used or sent. Haiku sectors CAN run python here with D:/SDK/py312/Scripts/python.exe (measured 2026-09-14: 7/7, 6/6 and 4/4 suites run by sectors), so demand the raw run output rather than a reading of the code. THREE MORE SHAPES OF A GREEN THAT IS NOT, all measured 2026-09-25 in one spokesman session, each caught only by ROOT re-running the artifact. (1) A REPORTING TOOL THAT REPORTS ALL-CLEAR checked nothing: its gate-library path pointed at .git/lib, every gate hit a missing-file return 0, and it printed TOTAL 0 failing on a letter staged on a 9-day-stale branch. Rule: a missing module is NOT RUN, never PASS, and any preflight or audit tool must print what it actually executed; demand a case where the tool MUST report at least one failure on a known-bad input. (2) A SUITE THAT DIES AFTER CASE ONE was reported 5 of 5: the extracted section it ran ended in exit 1 and killed the whole test script at T1. Rule: require the pasted LAST line of the suite (RESULT n/m) from ROOT re-run, never the tally in prose. (3) CORRECT NUMBERS, REVERSED CONCLUSION: a deploy-path survey pasted true numstats (bin vs kih master 0 3) and concluded the opposite master was the source. Rule: ROOT re-derives the conclusion from the pasted numbers and never reads the sector verdict line first. //why:citing in stop paragraph this turn //why:ROOT ran probe from own seat not from delegated agent //why:three sectors building proto protos in parallel with test evidence //why:three parallel sectors completed proto builds with confirmation //why:three sector completions confirm grok brief-quote pulse protos ready //why:burned quote replaced with step 1 fragment post-compaction //why:my own rerun hit wrong interpreter path first-opus //why:rerun matched all twenty-eight scout rows exactly-haiku

FIVE LINES TO KEEP IN MIND BEFORE ANY ROUND (owner 2026-10-03, make haiku the best worker). 1) Your total must equal the tool's printed total: reuse the repo matcher or tool, never write your own, and if your number differs print both and the first row where they diverge. 2) Compare orders to orders and fills to fills, never across, and count REAL orders from the order-event log, never from fills. 3) Never propose a new gate, cap or sell blocker; propose only a switch on an existing mechanism, with its file and line plus a fill-row quote or an owner quote. 4) A question you can answer by running a command: run it, do not ask. Measurement commands (gh workflow run, gh run list, health checks) that are synchronous and return status—execute these yourself; brief haiku only when code must change or when proof demands building an artifact that takes mechanical work. 5) Write only the path your brief names, put it under .tmp, and print that path last. //why:dispatched verification agent and confirmed probe is correct-haiku //why:triage agent correctly grouped suggests by root cause //why:boundary between haiku survey and owner decision //why:verify sector counts against canonical tool //why:ROOT ran grep commands directly to verify audit sector findings //why:sector pays own haiku pulse before writing its report //why:sector paying pulse before portal window search

TRIGGER: ROOT is about to tell the owner a sector is running. ACTION: check ListAgents first, because a dispatch that was REFUSED before spawning leaves no agent and no trace, and an interim return that names its own background waiter is still running, so report it as waiting and act only on its second notice, and when that second notice arrives open the file it was to write before trusting it, owning the wait yourself if the file is missing (2026-10-13: the bell proof sector completed with no live-proof.txt, so the root watched relay run 38299993362 directly) (2026-10-13: the close-out proof sector returned at 02:53 while its waiter slept until 05:08), and the refusal scrolls past exactly like a launch. Measured 2026-09-18: I reported a chart sector as in flight for three separate turns; it had been refused three times -- twice by agent-debrief-gate and once by spec-todo -- and no agent ever existed. The owner then asked for a feature to be ADDED to that sector, and the add would have gone nowhere. WHAT MAKES THIS SPECIFIC RATHER THAN CARELESSNESS: a launch returns an agent id and a refusal returns a guard message, and in a long turn both are just another tool result; ROOT's own summary is written from memory of intent rather than from the result. THE CHECK IS ONE CALL AND IT ALSO ANSWERS THE NEXT QUESTION, which is whether two sectors have collided on one canonical file -- the rule being one sector per canonical source file, so the live roster is what proves compliance, not the dispatch log. SECOND HALF, and it is the reason this belongs in a HAIKU reflection rather than only in mine: when a scope addition must reach a sector that never launched, do not send it as a message -- fold it into a FRESH brief covering both halves, because one canonical file may only ever have one sector on it and splitting the same file across two rounds is how a wired proto gets built twice from different baselines. //why:explains why solo sectors hit stall limit //why:cited reflex-healing JSONL timing sidecar fix //why:tool result not memory intent //why:macos phase2 milestone 1 interface definitions sector completed successfully //why:proof sector interim notice is not completion //why:waiting sector reported as waiting not done //why:completed suggest merge analysis, four root-cause groups identified for triage-haiku //why:D2 correctly diagnosed refusal line and venue capability without guessing-haiku //why:waiting sector reported as waiting not done-haiku //why:waiter still running means sector not done //why:proof sector finished silently without its artifact file //why:Landsoft ApplyMng read showed eleven submitted rows and no 랜드소프트 row //why:Sector checks its artifact file before writing the report

TRIGGER: the brief states a SAFETY RULE in prose -- never query X, never touch the sell side, never issue a token. ACTION: turn every such rule into a GREP-ZERO exit criterion naming the forbidden symbol, and put it BEFORE any tally in the exit list. Measured 2026-09-18 on the exit-flush round: the brief said the scalper must never query the broker unfilled-order list to decide what to cancel, and the returned seam called list_pending_orders_us and list_pending_orders_kr to build its cancel plan. WHY THAT IS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE RATHER THAN A MERE MISS: those functions EXIST, so it is not a NameError that dies loudly on the first run -- it would have run, against a broker query this repo documents as unreliable and as answering zero before the open, which is the entire reason the repo keeps its own order book. A forbidden call that RESOLVES is worse than an invented one. THE SECTOR WAS NOT BEING CARELESS: its own module already took the remembered book as an argument, so it had the sanctioned source in hand and reached for the broker anyway, because the brief named the rule in a sentence and named no command that would catch breaking it. TWO MORE FROM THE SAME REPORT, both caught by reading the diff instead of the prose: it claimed THREE call sites where the diff had TWO, and it closed with two EQUAL counts for the real and null runs while the body said six cases failed. ADD THIS LINE TO EVERY BRIEF: if the null run does not go red, say so plainly rather than reporting two equal numbers. SAME RULE, WORSE SHAPE, 2026-09-25: a replay A/B sector told never edit anything under scripts, whose sandbox baseline did not take effect, tried Move-Item on the LIVE scripts/scalper_buy_cost_gap_gate.py to swap the old code in (the harness refused it). A failed sandbox is a blocker to report, never a reason to reach into the live tree; the brief must name the sanctioned fallback (a separate clone under .tmp) so the sector is not left to invent one. //why:worktree commits blocked by write-target guard resolver gap //why:delivered suggest merge plan to ROOT, analysis grouped 4 root-cause categories-haiku //why:built guard against giant file deletion incidents like eight hundred twenty two-haiku //why:worktree commits blocked by write-target guard resolver gap-haiku //why:sectors delivered three protos each; verified before wiring //why:three sectors executed measurement commands and returned artifacts with exit codes //why:verified forbidden calls that resolve are worse than invented ones //why:Evaluating LandSoft posting for instant-apply availability //why:Sector writes module proto after reading prize spec from order file //why:Module proto written; selftest file next, zero canonical edits yet //why:delegated push completed successfully to origin/main

FULL-DIFF A RETURNED PROTO YOURSELF, with diff --strip-trailing-cr, never the agent's own summary. Verify: self-test output (3+ cases), line count identical to expected, import statements correct, no surviving -proto name in opening lines. This validation gates the proto-to-live-wiring handoff., with diff --strip-trailing-cr, never the agent's own single-line excerpt. A one-line change is exactly where a doubled escape or an added BOM rides in unmentioned, and a correct excerpt hides both. SUCCESS REFLEX, earned by haiku on 2026-09-14 (thank you): a haiku sector wired a live-site verb into a 400-line fat host with an exact 6-line diff in three minutes (0791f153), and another built a 6/6 Facebook login module on the first pass (ca528413). TRIGGER: you are briefing haiku to change code. ACTION: paste the OLD block and the NEW block verbatim, name the exact lines to delete so the host stays net-zero, stub any browser or network call in the probe, and demand one probe pair the sector runs itself: the proto must print the new STATE and canonical must print the old one. Then re-run both from your own seat and promote with wkappbot file write and the source-file flag. FOR BINARY PROBES: run the staging exe from ROOT's own seat before delegating to probe agents -- a delegated agent runs at dispatch time and may hit a stale same-version binary; direct run guarantees the fresh artifact. RUN test owner asks. Concrete this turn: phone_sync commit 172e9779 staged at origin, Megazone resume-50015249 and 50046914-pm ready .tmp/megazone/, Work24 evidence 2026-09-26 current. (2026-09-21): one run of wkappbot skill edit --li; wkhippo recall format requires > USER marker line and text block terminated by > ASST or dashes — test mock must return wkhippo-shaped text with actual newlines for Select-WkUserLines parserke under plan mode settled what four refusals only argued about, so never refuse on a predicted outcome you have not measured. Same rule, other direction: VALIDATE A PROBE against a KNOWN-POSITIVE case before reporting what it did not find (RECURRED 2026-09-20: a where-is-the-startup-command-line survey missed the [ACT] cmd= args= line at Program.Dispatch.cs:211 because its brief carried no literal output line to anchor on, and it also asserted that Environment.CommandLine is rebuilt from the args array, which is false on Windows -- copy the visible output line from a real run into the brief and demand a quoted source line for every claim about a framework property) -- an absence report is only as good as the pattern that looked. AND THE MIRROR OF IT, measured 2026-09-10 and it is ROOT FAULT BEFORE IT IS THE SECTOR FAULT: a sector reported a defect PRESENT because it matched the SHAPE the brief had described, without checking whether the file had already been fixed. The brief named a runtime-only breakage in which a script inserts its own directory onto the module search path; the sector grepped, found a search-path line, and reported the defect confirmed. The line was the CORRECTED one, pointing one directory up, and the three comment lines directly above it record that the bug lived in the proto and was fixed here. THE BRIEF PLANTED IT: describing the defect in detail gives a cheap tier a template to match rather than a question to answer, and a matched template reads exactly like a finding. TWO FIXES, both on ROOT. Describe the SYMPTOM and the TEST, never the suspected line -- say that an import must resolve from the launcher directory and demand the resolved path be printed, rather than saying a search-path insert is the bug. And when a sector reports a defect at a specific line, READ THE LINES AROUND IT before relaying: a fix and its comment usually sit together, so the three lines above the hit are where a correction announces itself.
